Bench-ready workflow for cloning a gene-of-interest PCR product into a plasmid, confirming the insert, preparing plasmid stocks, and aliquoting qPCR standards.

<div class="facts">
<div class="fact"><strong>Workflow</strong><span>Cloning to standards</span></div>
<div class="fact"><strong>Calendar time</strong><span>~4-7 d</span></div>
<div class="fact"><strong>Active time</strong><span>~12-17 h</span></div>
<div class="fact"><strong>Critical QC</strong><span>Colony PCR + Sanger</span></div>
</div>

---

## Before Starting

::: {.alert .alert-success role="alert"}
**Source status**

This page is the web-ready conversion of `Experiments Protocol-Gene cloning & qPCR Standards2025.docx`, with quick-reference notes from `gene cloning protocol.pdf`. When the DOCX and PDF differ, treat the DOCX workflow as the main source and treat the PDF values as lab-notebook variants to confirm before use.

:::
::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Contamination control**

Keep pre-PCR setup, post-PCR products, competent cells, and plasmid stocks physically separated when possible. Use sterile tips and fresh gloves when switching between PCR, cloning, transformation, and colony handling.

:::
::: {.alert .alert-danger role="alert"}
**Stop before changing selective conditions**

Confirm the vector, antibiotic, competent-cell type, primer pair, and expected insert size before beginning. Antibiotic concentration, vector choice, and colony selection criteria are not interchangeable.

:::
---

## Workflow Plan

| Day | Work |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Prepare LB plates and broth; amplify gene-of-interest; clean PCR product; quantify PCR product; set up ligation; incubate ligation overnight if needed. |
| Day 2 | Transform ligation into competent *E. coli*; plate on selective LB plates with X-Gal when blue-white screening is used; incubate overnight. |
| Day 3 | Screen 8-10 white colonies by colony PCR; run gel; start overnight colony culture or restreak selected colonies. |
| Day 4 | Make glycerol stocks; purify positive colony PCR products for Sanger sequencing or extract plasmid from positive cultures. |
| Day 5+ | Confirm sequence, quantify plasmid, dilute plasmid standards, aliquot qPCR standards, and store at -80 deg C. |

**Target qPCR standard stocks**

| Standard targets | Stock type | Typical amount |
|---|---|---|
| 16S, ITS, nifH, AOA/AOB/comx amoA, nirK/S, nosZI | *E. coli* stock | 4-5 tubes |
|  | Plasmid stock | 10 tubes, 50 uL each, 20-100 ng/uL |
|  | qPCR standard stock | 40-50 tubes, 20 uL each, 2-4 ng/uL |

**Check water volume**

If water becomes negative, reduce template or primer volume, or increase final reaction volume before preparing reactions.

## Ligation Insert Calculator

<div class="calculator-controls">
<div class="control">
<label for="insertSizeBp">Insert size (bp)</label>
<input id="insertSizeBp" type="number" min="1" step="1" value="600">
</div>
<div class="control">
<label for="vectorSizeBp">Vector size (bp)</label>
<input id="vectorSizeBp" type="number" min="1" step="1" value="3900">
</div>
<div class="control">
<label for="vectorMassNg">Vector mass (ng)</label>
<input id="vectorMassNg" type="number" min="1" step="1" value="50">
</div>
<div class="control">
<label for="insertConcNgUl">Purified PCR product concentration (ng/uL)</label>
<input id="insertConcNgUl" type="number" min="0.01" step="0.1" value="20">
</div>
</div>

| Ratio target | Insert mass | Insert volume at current concentration |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1:1 insert:vector | <span id="ligInsertMass1">7.7 ng</span> | <span id="ligInsertVol1">0.4 uL</span> |
| 3:1 insert:vector | <span id="ligInsertMass3">23.1 ng</span> | <span id="ligInsertVol3">1.2 uL</span> |

::: {.alert .alert-info role="alert"}
**Formula**

Insert mass for a 1:1 molar ratio is `(insert size bp x vector mass ng) / vector size bp`. The original notes recommend keeping insert:vector molar ratio between 1:3 and 3:1, with 1:1 often giving good results.

:::

## Part A: Prepare LB Plates and Broth

*~3-4 h elapsed; ~1-1.5 h active*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add tryptone, yeast extract, NaCl, and agar to less than 500 mL Milli-Q water in a 1 L bottle. For broth, omit agar.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Adjust to pH 7.0.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Autoclave at 121 deg C and 20 psi for at least 30 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Cool medium before adding antibiotic.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare kanamycin or ampicillin stock in the hood. For kanamycin, dissolve 50 mg in 1 mL water, mix well, and filter through a 0.22 um filter.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add antibiotic to cooled medium according to the vector and competent-cell workflow.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Pour about 25 plates from 500 mL medium in the hood.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare LB broth the same way, without agar.</span></li>
</ul>

![LB medium preparation](gene-cloning-qpcr-standards_assets/image1.png)

## Part B: Extract Template DNA

*~1.5-2 h*

Use this section when template DNA must be extracted before PCR.

| Material | Catalog # | Company |
|---|---|---|
| DNeasy PowerLyzer PowerSoil Kit | 12855-100 | Qiagen |

::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Before starting**

Perform centrifugation at room temperature. If Solution C1 has precipitated, heat at 60 deg C until dissolved. Shake Solution C4 before use.

:::
<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add up to 0.25 g soil sample to the PowerBead tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 750 uL PowerBead Solution.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 60 uL Solution C1 and invert several times or vortex briefly.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Balance tubes in the Fisherbrand Bead Mill 24 Homogenizer. Run PROG 01 (s=2.75, c=01, T=0.50, D=0.15) or PROG 02 (s=2.75, c=02, T=0.30, D=0.15).</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 30 s. Do not exceed 10,000 x g. For clay soils or incomplete pellets, centrifuge for 3 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Transfer supernatant to a clean 2 mL collection tube. Expect about 400-500 uL.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 250 uL Solution C2, vortex 5 s, and incubate at 2-8 deg C for 5 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge 1 min at 10,000 x g. Avoid the pellet and transfer up to 600 uL supernatant to a clean 2 mL tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 200 uL Solution C3, vortex briefly, and incubate at 2-8 deg C for 5 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge 1 min at 10,000 x g. Avoid the pellet and transfer up to 750 uL supernatant to a clean 2 mL tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 1200 uL Solution C4 and vortex 5 s.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Load 675 uL supernatant onto an MB Spin Column and centrifuge 1 min at 10,000 x g. Discard flow-through and repeat until all supernatant has passed through the column.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 500 uL Solution C5 and centrifuge 30 s at 10,000 x g.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Discard flow-through and centrifuge again for 1 min at 10,000 x g.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Place the spin filter in a clean 2 mL collection tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 100 uL Solution C6 to the center of the membrane and incubate 2 min. Sterile DNA-free PCR-grade water or TE buffer may be used instead.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge 30 s at 10,000 x g and discard the spin column.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part C: Amplify the Gene of Interest

*~3-4 h elapsed; ~1-1.5 h active*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Select primers for the gene of interest.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Dilute forward and reverse primers to 10 uM before use.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Set up PCR reactions using the calculator above or the source table below.</span></li>
</ul>

| Component | 50 uL reaction | 20 uL reaction |
|---|---:|---:|
| GoTaq Green Master Mix | 25 uL | 10 uL |
| Forward primer | 1 uL | 1 uL |
| Reverse primer | 1 uL | 1 uL |
| DNA | 2 uL | 2 uL |
| Water | To 50 uL | To 20 uL |

**Default PCR program from the DOCX source**

| Step | Temperature | Time | Cycles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial denaturation | 94 deg C | 3 min | 1 |
| Denaturation | 94 deg C | 1 min | 30 |
| Annealing | 50-60 deg C, usually 5 deg C below primer Tm | 1 min | 30 |
| Extension | 72 deg C | 1 min | 30 |
| Final extension | 72 deg C | 7 min | 1 |
| Hold | 4 deg C | Hold |  |

**Lab-notebook variant from PDF**

| Step | Temperature | Time | Cycles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial denaturation | 95 deg C | 5 min | 1 |
| Denaturation | 95 deg C | 30 s | 30 |
| Annealing | 59.2 deg C | 30 s | 30 |
| Extension | 72 deg C | 1 min | 30 |
| Final extension | 72 deg C | 5 min | 1 |
| Hold | 12 deg C | Hold |  |

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Run 5 uL PCR product on an agarose gel to confirm amplification.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>For a quick gel check, prepare 1.5-2% agarose for 500 bp to 10 kb fragments. A PDF note uses 2 g agarose per 100 mL buffer.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add gel stain according to the lab stock. The DOCX note uses 2.5 uL SYBR Safe in 50 mL gel; the PDF note uses 10 uL stain per 100 mL gel.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Run gel at 50-100 V for 20-30 min, or until the dye front reaches about two-thirds of the tray.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Image the gel on the Bio-Rad GelDoc Go using the appropriate stain setting.</span></li>
</ul>

![PCR gel check example](gene-cloning-qpcr-standards_assets/image2.png)

---

## Part D: Purify PCR Product

*~30-45 min*

| Material | Catalog # | Company |
|---|---|---|
| QIAquick PCR Purification Kit | 28104 | Qiagen |

::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Before starting**

Add ethanol to Buffer PE before use and mark the bottle. Carry out centrifugation at room temperature. The source DOCX lists 13,000 rpm for tabletop microcentrifuge steps.

:::
<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 5 volumes Buffer PB to 1 volume PCR reaction and mix.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Place a QIAquick column in the provided 2 mL collection tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Apply sample to the column and centrifuge 30-60 s until the sample has passed through.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Discard flow-through and place the column back into the same collection tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 750 uL Buffer PE and centrifuge 30-60 s.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Discard flow-through and centrifuge 1 min to remove residual wash buffer.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Place the column in a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Elute DNA with 50 uL Buffer EB or water. For increased concentration, use 30 uL, let stand 1 min, then centrifuge.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>If running purified DNA on a gel, add 1 volume loading dye to 5 volumes purified DNA.</span></li>
</ul>

::: {.alert .alert-info role="alert"}
**Gel purification option**

If non-target bands are present, cut the correct band from the gel and use a gel purification kit such as QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit, catalog 28704.

:::
---

## Part E: Ligate PCR Product into Vector

*~30-60 min active; overnight optional*

| Material | Catalog # | Company |
|---|---|---|
| TA Cloning Kit with pCR 2.1 Vector | K204001 | ThermoFisher Scientific |
| Promega pGEM T-Easy Vector | Use for bacterial 16S primers if needed | Promega |

::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Fresh PCR product**

Use fresh PCR product when possible. The DOCX notes that single 3 prime A-overhangs degrade over time, reducing ligation efficiency.

:::
<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge one vial of vector briefly to collect liquid at the bottom.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Use the calculator above to estimate insert mass and insert volume.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Do not use more than 2-3 uL PCR sample in the ligation reaction unless confirmed, because salts in PCR sample may inhibit T4 DNA ligase.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Target insert:vector molar ratio between 1:3 and 3:1. A 1:1 ratio often gives good results.</span></li>
</ul>

| Ligation component | Standard reaction |
|---|---:|
| Fresh purified PCR product | x uL, often 4-5 uL if concentration allows |
| 5X T4 DNA Ligase Reaction Buffer | 2 uL |
| pCR 2.1 vector, 25 ng/uL | 2 uL |
| T-Easy vector, 50 ng/uL | 1 uL if using pGEM T-Easy workflow |
| Water | To 9 uL before ligase |
| ExpressLink T4 DNA Ligase, 5 units | 1 uL |
| **Final volume** | **10 uL** |

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Assemble ligation reaction on ice or according to kit guidance.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Incubate at room temperature for at least 15 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>For higher efficiency, incubate up to 1 h or overnight when appropriate.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Store ligation at -20 deg C if transformation will not be done immediately.</span></li>
</ul>

**PDF lab-notebook ligation variant**

| Component | Volume |
|---|---:|
| PCR product | 2.5 uL |
| T4 DNA Ligase | 1 uL |
| T-Easy Vector | 1 uL |
| Ligation buffer | 5 uL |
| DI water | 0.5 uL |
| **Final volume** | **10 uL** |

::: {.alert .alert-info role="alert"}
**16S note**

The DOCX notes: use GoTaq Green PCR Master Mix, pGEM T-Easy Vector, and JMP competent cells for cloning bacterial 16S amplicons. Other amplicons may use either ligation and cloning product set. Confirm vector and cell choice before starting.

:::
---

## Part F: Transform into Competent E. coli

*~18-24 h elapsed; ~1-1.5 h active*

| Material | Catalog # | Company |
|---|---|---|
| One Shot TOP10 Chemically Competent *E. coli* | K204001 | ThermoFisher Scientific |

::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Before starting**

Equilibrate a water bath to 42 deg C. Bring S.O.C. medium to room temperature. Equilibrate selective LB plates at 37 deg C for 30 min. Spread each plate with 40 uL of 40 mg/mL X-Gal and let it soak in when blue-white screening is used.

:::
<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge ligation vials briefly and place on ice.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Thaw one 50 uL vial of frozen competent cells on ice for each transformation.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Pipette 2 uL ligation reaction directly into competent cells and mix gently with the pipette tip.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Incubate on ice for 30 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Heat-shock at 42 deg C without shaking. DOCX uses 30 s; PDF note uses 45 s. Confirm before running.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Immediately transfer cells to ice.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add recovery medium. DOCX uses 250 uL S.O.C.; PDF note uses 950 uL LB medium. Confirm the chosen competent-cell protocol.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Shake horizontally at 37 deg C and 225 rpm. DOCX uses 1 h; PDF note uses 90 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Spread 10-200 uL from each transformation on selective LB agar with X-Gal and either 50 ug/mL kanamycin or 100 ug/mL ampicillin.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Plate at least two volumes so one plate has well-spaced colonies. For small volumes, add 20 uL S.O.C. to spread evenly.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Incubate plates overnight at 37 deg C.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Transfer plates to 4 deg C for 2-3 h to allow proper color development.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Pick at least 10 white colonies and grow each on a new plate and/or 2-5 mL selective LB broth overnight.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part G: Screen Colonies by Colony PCR

*~3-4 h elapsed; ~1-1.5 h active*

| Material | Catalog # | Company |
|---|---|---|
| LB plates with antibiotic and X-Gal |  | Lab-made |
| Sterile toothpicks or sterile tips |  | Lab stock |

**M13 colony PCR reaction**

| Component | Volume |
|---|---:|
| Taq polymerase or master mix | 15 uL |
| Forward primer | 0.6 uL |
| Reverse primer | 0.6 uL |
| Water | 13.8 uL |
| Colony DNA | Touch a colony with sterile toothpick or tip and transfer to PCR tube |
| **Final volume** | **30 uL** |

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Pick 8-10 white colonies for screening.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Touch each colony with a sterile toothpick or pipette tip and transfer to the assigned PCR tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Run M13 PCR: 94 deg C for 1 min; then 30 cycles of 98 deg C for 5 s, 55 deg C for 5 s, and 72 deg C for 40 s.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Run 5 uL of each reaction on a 1% agarose gel.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Select colonies with the expected insert band for Sanger sequencing and plasmid stock preparation.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part H: Sanger Sequencing

*~15-30 min active; ~1-3 business days turnaround*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Purify positive colony PCR products using the PCR purification section above.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare each sample according to the sequencing provider requirements. The source notes refer to Azenta Life Sciences / Genewiz.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>For pCR 2.1 insert sequencing, prepare a premix of purified PCR product and M13R primer, or the provider-requested single primer.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Record sample name, primer, expected insert size, concentration, and submission ID.</span></li>
</ul>

::: {.alert .alert-info role="alert"}
**PDF note**

The PDF note says Sanger samples should be about 1 ng/uL, 10 uL sample, with 5 uL of 5 nM forward primer. Confirm current provider requirements before submission.

:::
---

## Part I: Quantify DNA by Qubit

*~30-45 min*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Set up the required number of Qubit tubes for samples and the 2 standards.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Use thin-wall, clear 0.5 mL Qubit assay tubes for the Qubit 4 Fluorometer.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Label tube lids, not tube sides.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare Qubit working solution with 199 uL buffer and 1 uL reagent per tube, or use the calculator above.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 190 uL working solution plus 10 uL standard to each standard tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 198 uL working solution plus 2 uL sample to each user sample tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Vortex 3-5 s without making bubbles.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Incubate at room temperature for 2 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>On the Qubit home screen, select dsDNA, then dsDNA High Sensitivity.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Read Standard 1 and Standard 2 when prompted.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Select sample volume and units, then read each sample tube.</span></li>
</ul>

![Qubit working solution reference](gene-cloning-qpcr-standards_assets/image3.png)

## Part J: Prepare Plasmid Stock and qPCR Standards

*~1-2 d elapsed; ~3-5 h active*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Spread each prepared LB plate with 40 uL of 40 mg/mL X-Gal and let liquid soak in.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Streak *E. coli* with confirmed correct inserts onto selective LB agar with X-Gal and the correct antibiotic.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Incubate at 37 deg C for 24 h.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Scrape and collect biomass into microcentrifuge tubes.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Extract plasmid using QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit.</span></li>
</ul>

### QIAprep Plasmid Purification

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Resuspend pelleted bacterial cells in 250 uL Buffer P1 and transfer to a microcentrifuge tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 250 uL Buffer P2 and mix by inverting 4-6 times until clear. Do not let lysis proceed for more than 5 min.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add 350 uL Buffer N3 and immediately invert 4-6 times.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge for 10 min at 13,000 rpm.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Apply 800 uL supernatant to the QIAprep 2.0 spin column and centrifuge 30-60 s. Discard flow-through.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Wash with 0.5 mL Buffer PB, centrifuge 30-60 s, and discard flow-through.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Wash with 0.75 mL Buffer PE, centrifuge 30-60 s, and discard flow-through.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Centrifuge 1 min to remove residual wash buffer.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Place column in a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Elute with 50 uL Buffer EB or water. Let stand 1 min and centrifuge 1 min.</span></li>
</ul>

### Plasmid Copy Number

Use this formula:

```text
copy number per uL =
(plasmid concentration ng/uL x 6.022e23) /
(plasmid size bp x 650 g/mol x 1e9)
```

Where:

- Plasmid concentration is in ng/uL.
- Plasmid size is in bp.
- 650 g/mol is the average molecular weight of a double-stranded DNA base pair.
- 1e9 converts ng to g.

### Aliquot qPCR Standards

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Gather the required *E. coli* stock, plasmid stock, and standard stock tubes before dilution.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Dilute plasmid stock to a final concentration of 2-4 ng/uL, using the calculator above when helpful.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Aliquot 20 uL plasmid standard into 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare 40-50 qPCR standard tubes when making the routine standard stock set.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Store qPCR standards at -80 deg C.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part K: Optional Restriction Digest of Plasmid DNA

*~2-3 h elapsed; ~1-1.5 h active*

Reference: [Addgene restriction digest protocol](https://www.addgene.org/protocols/restriction-digest/)

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Select restriction enzyme or enzymes for the plasmid.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Check the plasmid vector map or analyze the sequence with Addgene Sequence Analyzer.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Determine the correct reaction buffer. For double digests, use an enzyme compatibility chart such as NEB Double Digest Finder.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare a 50 uL reaction with 1 ug DNA, 1 uL of each restriction enzyme, 5 uL 10X buffer, and water to 50 uL.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Mix gently by pipetting.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Incubate at the enzyme-appropriate temperature, usually 37 deg C, for 1 h or overnight.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Purify the digest with a DNA cleanup kit if needed.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Visualize digest by 1% agarose gel electrophoresis for about 40 min.</span></li>
</ul>

## Lab Notebook Quick Reference

These notes came from `gene cloning protocol.pdf`. Use them as a quick reference, not as a replacement for the main workflow.

| Stage | Notebook note |
|---|---|
| PCR | 20 uL reaction: 10 uL master mix, 7 uL DI water, 1 uL primer mix, 2 uL DNA. Program: 95 deg C 5 min; 30 cycles of 95 deg C 30 s, 59.2 deg C 30 s, 72 deg C 1 min; 72 deg C 5 min; hold 12 deg C. |
| Gel | 2% gel: 2 g agarose per 100 mL buffer; 10 uL gel dye per 100 mL gel. Load 1 uL dye, 1 uL ladder or 5 uL sample, and 3 uL DI water as noted. |
| PCR purification | Use all PCR sample when needed; Buffer PB = 5 x sample volume; wash with 750 uL PE; elute with 30 uL EB. |
| Ligation | Notebook example: 2.5 uL PCR product, 1 uL T4 DNA Ligase, 1 uL T-Easy Vector, 5 uL ligation buffer, 0.5 uL DI water. |
| Transformation | Notebook variant: 50 uL competent cells, 2 uL ligation, ice 30 min, 42 deg C for 45 s, 950 uL LB, shake at 225 rpm for 90 min, plate and incubate overnight at 37 deg C. |
| Colony PCR | Same as regular PCR but notebook note says 19 cycles. Confirm before use. |
| Plasmid stock | Collect colony biomass from plates, extract plasmid, quantify by NanoDrop, dilute to 2-4 ng/uL, prepare 40 tubes of 20 uL standards. |
| Glycerol stock | Mix 500 uL 50% glycerol solution with 500 uL colony culture in screw-cap tube and store at -80 deg C. |

## Stop Points

::: {.alert .alert-danger role="alert"}
**Stop and ask before**

- Using a different vector, competent-cell strain, antibiotic, or blue-white screening setup than planned.
- Proceeding when PCR gives non-specific bands or no expected band.
- Ligating an old PCR product without confirming that the vector workflow tolerates it.
- Transforming before confirming the recovery medium, heat-shock time, antibiotic, and X-Gal setup.
- Picking blue colonies when blue-white screening is being used for insert selection.
- Sending Sanger samples without recording primer, expected insert size, sample concentration, and submission ID.
- Diluting qPCR standards when plasmid concentration, plasmid size, or target standard concentration is uncertain.
- Treating the PDF quick-reference parameters as the active protocol when they conflict with the DOCX workflow.

:::
<script>
(function () {
  const pcrReactionCount = document.getElementById("pcrReactionCount");
  const pcrReactionVolume = document.getElementById("pcrReactionVolume");
  const pcrTemplateVolume = document.getElementById("pcrTemplateVolume");
  const insertSizeBp = document.getElementById("insertSizeBp");
  const vectorSizeBp = document.getElementById("vectorSizeBp");
  const vectorMassNg = document.getElementById("vectorMassNg");
  const insertConcNgUl = document.getElementById("insertConcNgUl");
  const qubitSampleCount = document.getElementById("qubitSampleCount");
  const stockConcNgUl = document.getElementById("stockConcNgUl");
  const targetConcNgUl = document.getElementById("targetConcNgUl");
  const finalStandardVolume = document.getElementById("finalStandardVolume");
  const labNotes = document.getElementById("labNotes");
  const clearNotes = document.getElementById("clearNotes");
  const notesStatus = document.getElementById("notesStatus");
  const notesStorageKey = "gene-cloning-qpcr-standards-notes";

  function el(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function setText(id, text) { const node = el(id); if (node) node.textContent = text; }
  function number(input, fallback, min) {
    const value = parseFloat(input.value);
    return Math.max(min, Number.isFinite(value) ? value : fallback);
  }
  function whole(input, fallback, min) {
    const value = parseInt(input.value, 10);
    return Math.max(min, Number.isFinite(value) ? value : fallback);
  }
  function fmtVol(value) {
    if (value < 0) return "Check recipe";
    if (value < 0.01) return "<0.01 uL";
    if (value < 1) return value.toFixed(2) + " uL";
    return (Number.isInteger(value) ? value : value.toFixed(1)) + " uL";
  }
  function fmtMass(value) {
    if (value < 0.01) return "<0.01 ng";
    return (Number.isInteger(value) ? value : value.toFixed(1)) + " ng";
  }

  function updatePcr() {
    const n = whole(pcrReactionCount, 1, 1);
    const finalVol = number(pcrReactionVolume, 20, 1);
    const template = number(pcrTemplateVolume, 2, 0);
    const master = finalVol / 2;
    const forward = 1;
    const reverse = 1;
    const water = finalVol - master - forward - reverse - template;
    const rows = [
      ["pcrMaster", master],
      ["pcrForward", forward],
      ["pcrReverse", reverse],
      ["pcrTemplate", template],
      ["pcrWater", water],
      ["pcrFinal", finalVol]
    ];
    rows.forEach(function (row) {
      const id = row[0];
      const per = row[1];
      setText(id + "Per", fmtVol(per));
      setText(id + "Total", fmtVol(per * n));
      setText(id + "Extra", fmtVol(per * n * 1.1));
    });
  }

  function updateLigation() {
    const insert = number(insertSizeBp, 600, 1);
    const vector = number(vectorSizeBp, 3900, 1);
    const vectorMass = number(vectorMassNg, 50, 0.01);
    const conc = number(insertConcNgUl, 20, 0.01);
    const mass1 = insert * vectorMass / vector;
    const mass3 = mass1 * 3;
    setText("ligInsertMass1", fmtMass(mass1));
    setText("ligInsertMass3", fmtMass(mass3));
    setText("ligInsertVol1", fmtVol(mass1 / conc));
    setText("ligInsertVol3", fmtVol(mass3 / conc));
  }

  function updateQubit() {
    const samples = whole(qubitSampleCount, 8, 1);
    const tubes = samples + 2 + 2;
    setText("qubitTubeCount", String(tubes));
    setText("qubitTubeCount2", String(tubes));
    setText("qubitTubeCount3", String(tubes));
    setText("qubitBufferTotal", fmtVol(tubes * 199));
    setText("qubitReagentTotal", fmtVol(tubes));
    setText("qubitWorkingTotal", fmtVol(tubes * 200));
  }

  function updateStandardDilution() {
    const stock = number(stockConcNgUl, 100, 0.01);
    const target = number(targetConcNgUl, 3, 0.01);
    const finalVol = number(finalStandardVolume, 1000, 1);
    const stockVol = target <= stock ? finalVol * target / stock : -1;
    const diluent = stockVol >= 0 ? finalVol - stockVol : -1;
    setText("stdStockVolume", fmtVol(stockVol));
    setText("stdDiluentVolume", fmtVol(diluent));
    setText("stdFinalVolume", fmtVol(finalVol));
  }

  function initNotes() {
    try { labNotes.value = localStorage.getItem(notesStorageKey) || ""; } catch (e) {}
    labNotes.addEventListener("input", function () {
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(notesStorageKey, labNotes.value);
        notesStatus.textContent = "Saved locally in this browser.";
      } catch (e) {
        notesStatus.textContent = "Could not save notes.";
      }
    });
    clearNotes.addEventListener("click", function () {
      labNotes.value = "";
      try {
        localStorage.removeItem(notesStorageKey);
        notesStatus.textContent = "Notes cleared.";
      } catch (e) {}
    });
  }

  [pcrReactionCount, pcrReactionVolume, pcrTemplateVolume].forEach(function (input) {
    input.addEventListener("input", updatePcr);
  });
  [insertSizeBp, vectorSizeBp, vectorMassNg, insertConcNgUl].forEach(function (input) {
    input.addEventListener("input", updateLigation);
  });
  qubitSampleCount.addEventListener("input", updateQubit);
  [stockConcNgUl, targetConcNgUl, finalStandardVolume].forEach(function (input) {
    input.addEventListener("input", updateStandardDilution);
  });

  initNotes();
  updatePcr();
  updateLigation();
  updateQubit();
  updateStandardDilution();
})();
</script>
